Main.sentence: Islamabad ( /ɪzˈlɑːməbæd/ ⓘ ;  ___E:Urdu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urdu_language)___ : اسلام‌آباد , romanized: Islāmābād , lit. 'City of ___E:Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam)___ ', [ɪsˈlɑːmɑːbɑːd] ⓘ ) is the ___E:capital city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_city)___ of ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan)___ .

It is the country's ___E:tenth-most populous city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Pakistan_by_population)___ with a population of over 1.1 million, and is federally administered by the ___E:Pakistani government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Pakistan)___ as part of the ___E:Islamabad Capital Territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Capital_Territory)___ .

Built as a ___E:planned city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planned_city)___ in the 1960s and established in 1967, it replaced ___E:Karachi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karachi)___ as Pakistan's national capital.

The Greek architect ___E:Constantinos Apostolou Doxiadis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantinos_Apostolou_Doxiadis)___ developed Islamabad's ___E:master plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planned_community)___ , in which he divided it into eight zones; the city comprises administrative, ___E:diplomatic enclave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_Enclave,_Islamabad)___ , residential areas, educational and industrial sectors, commercial areas, as well as rural and green areas administered by the ___E:Islamabad Metropolitan Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Metropolitan_Corporation)___ with support from the ___E:Capital Development Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_Development_Authority_(Islamabad))___ .

Islamabad is known for its parks and forests, including the ___E:Margalla Hills National Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margalla_Hills_National_Park)___ and the ___E:Shakarparian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakarparian)___ .
It is home to several landmarks, including the country's flagship ___E:Faisal Mosque U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faisal_Mosque)___ .

Other prominent landmarks include the ___E:Pakistan Monument U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Monument)___ and ___E:Democracy Square U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D-Chowk_(Islamabad))___ .

Rated as ___E:Gamma + U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globalization_and_World_Cities_Research_Network#Gamma_+)___ by the ___E:Globalization and World Cities Research Network U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globalization_and_World_Cities_Research_Network)___ ,  Islamabad has one of the highest ___E:costs of living U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costs_of_living)___ in Pakistan.
The city's populace is dominated by both middle- and upper-middle-class citizens.

Islamabad is home to more than twenty universities, including ___E:Bahria University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahria_University)___ , ___E:Quaid-e-Azam University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaid-i-Azam_University)___ , ___E:PIEAS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Institute_of_Engineering_and_Applied_Sciences)___ , ___E:COMSATS University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COMSATS_University_Islamabad)___ , and ___E:NUST U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_Sciences_%26_Technology)___ .

It is also rated as one of the safest cities in Pakistan and has an expansive ___E:RFID U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio-frequency_identification)___ -enabled surveillance system with almost 2,000 active ___E:CCTV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closed-circuit_television)___ cameras.
The name Islamabad means City of Islam .
It is derived from two words; Islam and abad .

The Arabic word Islam means "submission [to God]" as it refers to the religion of ___E:Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam)___ , Pakistan's ___E:state religion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_religion)___ , and the ___E:Persian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_language)___ suffix -abad means cultivated place , indicating an inhabited place or city.  During the course of early modern period, the name was used in the ___E:Mughal era U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_era)___ , by the emperor ___E:Aurangzeb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurangzeb)___ who named many towns in the Indian subcontinent after it.  [c] According to a history book by ___E:Muhammad Ismail Zabeeh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ismail_Zabeeh)___ , teacher and poet ___E:Qazi Abdur Rehman Amritsari U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qazi_Abdur_Rehman_Amritsari)___ proposed the name of the city.
Occasionally in writing, Islamabad is colloquially abbreviated ISB .

Such usage originated in ___E:SMS language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SMS_language)___ , in part due to the ___E:IATA location identifier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IATA_location_identifier)___ for the ___E:Islamabad International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_International_Airport)___ .

___E:Islamabad Capital Territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Capital_Territory)___ , located on the ___E:Pothohar Plateau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pothohar_Plateau)___ of the northern ___E:Punjab region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_region)___ , is considered one of the earliest sites of human settlement in Asia. Some of the earliest ___E:Stone Age U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_Age)___ artefacts in the world have been found on the plateau, dating from 100,000 to 500,000 years ago. Rudimentary stones recovered from the terraces of the ___E:Soan River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soan_River)___ testify to the endeavours of early man in the ___E:inter-glacial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glacial_period)___ period.
Items of pottery and utensils dating back to prehistory have been found.

Excavations by Dr. Abdul Ghafoor Lone reveal evidence of a prehistoric culture in the area. Relics and human skulls have been found dating back to 5000 BCE that indicate the region was home to ___E:Neolithic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neolithic)___ peoples who settled on the banks of the Soan  and who later developed small communities in the region around 3000 BCE.

The ___E:Indus Valley civilization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indus_Valley_civilization)___ flourished in the region between the 23rd and 18th centuries BCE. Later the area was an early settlement of the ___E:Aryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aryan)___ community ___E:which migrated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Aryan_migrations)___ into the region from ___E:Central Asia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Asia)___ .

Many great armies such as those of ___E:Zahiruddin Babur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zahiruddin_Babur)___ , ___E:Genghis Khan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genghis_Khan)___ , ___E:Timur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timur)___ and ___E:Ahmad Shah Durrani U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Shah_Durrani)___ crossed the region during their invasions of the ___E:Indian subcontinent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_subcontinent)___ .

In 2015–16, the Federal Department of Archaeology and Museums, with the financial support of National Fund for Cultural Heritage, carried out initial archaeological excavations and unearthed the remains of a Buddhist stupa at Ban Faqiran, near the ___E:Shah Allah Ditta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Allah_Ditta)___ caves.
The stupa was dated to between the 2nd and 4th centuries CE.
When Pakistan gained independence in 1947, the southern port city of ___E:Karachi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karachi)___ was its provisional national capital.

In 1958, a commission was constituted to select a suitable site near ___E:Rawalpindi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawalpindi)___ for the national capital with particular emphasis on location, climate, logistics, and defence requirements, along with other attributes.

After extensive study, research, and a thorough review of potential sites, the commission recommended the area northeast of Rawalpindi in 1959 which was used as provisional capital from that year on.   In the 1960s, Islamabad was constructed as a ___E:forward capital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_city#capital_as_symbol)___ for several reasons.
Karachi was also located at the southern end of the country along the ___E:Arabian Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Sea)___ .
Pakistan needed a capital that was easily accessible from all parts of the country.
Karachi, a business centre, was also considered unsuitable partly because of intervention of business interests in government affairs.

The newly selected location of Islamabad was closer to the ___E:army headquarters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Headquarters_(Pakistan_Army))___ in Rawalpindi and the Pakistani-administered sectors of the disputed ___E:Kashmir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmir)___ in the north.

A Greek firm of architects, led by ___E:Konstantinos Apostolos Doxiadis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konstantinos_Apostolos_Doxiadis)___ , designed the master plan of the city based on a ___E:grid plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grid_plan)___ which was triangular in shape with its apex towards the ___E:Margalla Hills U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margalla_Hills)___ .

Islamabad was touted by Pakistani legislators as their counterpart to ___E:Chandigarh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandigarh)___ , whose ___E:modernism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modernism_(architecture))___ they envied and with which it shares conceptual similarities.

The capital was not moved directly from Karachi to Islamabad; it was first shifted temporarily to Rawalpindi in the early 1960s and then to Islamabad when essential development work was completed in 1966.  In 1981, Islamabad separated from Punjab province to form Capital Territory.

Such world-renowned architects as ___E:Edward Durell Stone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Durell_Stone)___ and ___E:Gio Ponti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gio_Ponti)___ have been associated with the city's development.
Islamabad has attracted people from all over Pakistan, making it one of the most cosmopolitan and urbanised cities of Pakistan.

As the capital city it has hosted numerous important meetings, such as the ___E:South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asian_Association_for_Regional_Cooperation)___ summit in 2004.

The city suffered damage from the ___E:2005 Kashmir earthquake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Kashmir_earthquake)___ which had a magnitude of 7.6.  Islamabad has experienced a series of terrorist incidents including the July 2007 ___E:Siege of Lal Masjid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Lal_Masjid)___ (Red Mosque), the June 2008 ___E:Danish embassy bombing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Danish_embassy_bombing_in_Islamabad)___ , and the September 2008 ___E:Marriott bombing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Marriott_Hotel_bombing)___ .
In 2011, four terrorist incidents occurred in the city, killing four people, including the murder of the Punjab Governor ___E:Salmaan Taseer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salmaan_Taseer)___ .

Construction of the ___E:Rawalpindi-Islamabad Metrobus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawalpindi-Islamabad_Metrobus)___ , the region's first mass transit line, began in February 2014 and was completed in March 2015. The Rawalpindi Development Authority built the project at a cost of approximately Rs. 24 billion, which was shared by both the Federal government and the provincial government of Punjab.

Islamabad lies about 540 metres (1,770 ft) above sea level at the northern edge of the ___E:Pothohar Plateau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pothohar_Plateau)___ and at the foot of the Margalla Hills in ___E:Islamabad Capital Territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Capital_Territory)___ .

The modern capital and the ancient ___E:Gakhar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gakhars)___ city of Rawalpindi form a ___E:conurbation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conurbation)___ and are commonly referred to as the Twin Cities.

To the northeast of the city lies the colonial era hill station of ___E:Murree U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murree)___ , and to the north lies the ___E:Haripur District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haripur_District)___ of ___E:Khyber Pakhtunkhwa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khyber_Pakhtunkhwa)___ . ___E:Kahuta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kahuta)___ lies on the southeast, ___E:Taxila U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxila)___ , ___E:Wah Cantt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wah_Cantt)___ , and ___E:Attock District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attock_District)___ to the northwest, ___E:Gujar Khan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujar_Khan)___ , Rawat, and ___E:Mandrah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandrah)___ on the southeast, and the metropolis of ___E:Rawalpindi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawalpindi)___ to the south and southwest.

Islamabad is located 120 kilometres (75 mi) southwest of ___E:Muzaffarabad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muzaffarabad)___ , 185 kilometres (115 mi) east of ___E:Peshawar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshawar)___ and 295 kilometres (183 mi) northwest of ___E:Lahore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore)___ .
Islamabad covers an area of 906 square kilometres (350 sq mi).
A further 2,717 square kilometres (1,049 sq mi) area is known as the Specified Area, with the Margala Hills in the north and northeast.
The southern portion of the city is an undulating plain.

It is drained by the ___E:Kurang River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korang_River)___ , on which the ___E:Rawal Dam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawal_lake#Features_of_Rawal_Lake_dam)___ is located.

Islamabad has a ___E:humid subtropical climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate)___ ( ___E:Köppen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification)___ : Cwa), with five seasons: Winter (November–February), Spring (March and April), Summer (May and June), Rainy Monsoon (July and August) and Autumn (September and October).
The hottest month is June, where average highs routinely exceed 38 °C (100.4 °F).

The wettest month is July, with heavy rainfalls and evening ___E:thunderstorms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderstorms)___ with the possibility of ___E:cloudburst U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloudburst)___ and flooding.
The coolest month is January.

Islamabad's ___E:micro-climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro-climate)___ is regulated by three artificial reservoirs: ___E:Rawal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawal_Lake)___ , ___E:Simli U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simli_Lake&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , and ___E:Khanpur Dam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanpur_Dam)___ .

The latter is located on the ___E:Haro River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haro_River)___ near the town of ___E:Khanpur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khanpur_(NWFP))___ , about 40 kilometres (25 mi) from Islamabad.
Simli Dam is 30 kilometres (19 mi) north of Islamabad. 220 acres (89 ha) of the city consists of ___E:Margalla Hills National Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margalla_Hills_National_Park)___ .
Loi Bher Forest is situated along the ___E:Islamabad Highway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Highway)___ , covering an area of 1,087 acres (440 ha).
The highest monthly rainfall of 743.3 mm (29.26 in) was recorded during July 1995.  Winters generally feature dense fog in the mornings and sunny afternoons.

In the city, temperatures stay mild, with snowfall over the higher-elevation points on nearby hill stations, notably ___E:Murree U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murree)___ and ___E:Nathia Gali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathia_Gali)___ .

The temperatures range from 13 °C (55 °F) in January to 38 °C (100 °F) in June. The highest recorded temperature was 46.6 °C (115.9 °F) on 23 June 2005 while the lowest temperature was −6.0 °C (21.2 °F) on 17 January 1967.   Light snowfall sometimes happens on the peaks of the hills visible from the city, though this is rare.  Snowfall does not occur in the city itself.
On 23 July 2001, Islamabad received a record-breaking 620 mm (24 in) of rainfall in just 10 hours.

It was the heaviest rainfall in Islamabad in the past 100 years and the highest rainfall in 24 hours as well.   Water supply is strained, leading to project proposals like the ___E:Ghazi Barotha water supply project U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghazi_Barotha_water_supply_project)___ .

The ___E:Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICT_Administration)___ , generally known as ICT Administration, is the civil administration as well as main law and order agency of the federal capital.

The local government authority of the city is the ___E:Islamabad Metropolitan Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Metropolitan_Corporation)___ (IMC) with some help from Capital Development Authority (CDA), which oversees the planning, development, construction, and administration of the city.   Islamabad Capital Territory is divided into eight zones: Administrative Zone, Commercial District, Educational Sector, Industrial Sector, Diplomatic Enclave, Residential Areas, Rural Areas and Green Area.  Islamabad city is divided into five major zones: Zone I, Zone II, Zone III, Zone IV, and Zone V. Out of these, Zone IV is the largest in area.  Zone I consists mainly of all the developed residential sectors while Zone II consists of the under-developed residential sectors.

Each residential sector is identified by a letter of the alphabet and a number, and covers an area of approximately 2 km × 2 km ( .mw-parser-output .frac{white-space:nowrap}.mw-parser-output .frac .num,.mw-parser-output .frac .den{font-size:80%;line-height:0;vertical-align:super}.mw-parser-output .frac .den{vertical-align:sub}.mw-parser-output .sr-only{border:0;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);clip-path:polygon(0px 0px,0px 0px,0px 0px);height:1px;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:absolute;width:1px} 1+1⁄4 mi × 1+1⁄4 mi).
The sectors are lettered from A to I, and each sector is divided into four numbered sub-sectors.
Series A, B, and C are still underdeveloped.
The D series has seven sectors (D-11 to D-17),  of which only sector D-12 is completely developed.
This series is located at the foot of Margalla Hills.
The E Sectors are named from E-7 to E-17.  Many foreigners and diplomatic personnel are housed in these sectors.

In the revised Master Plan of the city, CDA has decided to develop a park on the pattern of ___E:Fatima Jinnah Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatima_Jinnah_Park)___ in sector E-14. Sectors E-8 and E-9 contain the campuses of ___E:Bahria University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahria_University)___ , ___E:Air University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_University_(Pakistan))___ , and the ___E:National Defence University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Defence_University,_Pakistan)___ .
The F and G series contains the most developed sectors.
F series contains sectors F-5 to F-17; some sectors are still under-developed.

F-5 is an important sector for the software industry in Islamabad, as the two software technology parks are located here. The entire F-9 sector is covered with Fatima Jinnah Park. The ___E:Centaurus complex U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Centaurus_(building))___ is a major landmark of the F-8 sector.

G sectors are numbered G-5 through G-17.  Some important places include the ___E:Jinnah Convention Centre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinnah_Convention_Centre)___ and ___E:Serena Hotel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serena_Hotels)___ in G-5, the ___E:Lal Masjid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lal_Masjid,_Islamabad)___ in G-6, the ___E:Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Institute_of_Medical_Sciences)___ , the largest medical complex in the capital, located in G-8,  and the Karachi Company shopping center in G-9.

The H sectors are numbered H-8 through H-17.  The H sectors are mostly dedicated to educational and health institutions. ___E:National University of Sciences and Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_Sciences_and_Technology,_Pakistan)___ covers a major portion of sector H-12.  The I sectors are numbered from I-8 to I-18. With the exception of I-8, which is a well-developed residential area, these sectors are primarily part of the industrial zone. Two sub-sectors of I-9 and one sub-sector of ___E:I-10 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I-10,_Islamabad)___ are used as industrial areas.

CDA is planning to set up Islamabad Railway Station in Sector I-18 and Industrial City in sector I-17.  Zone III consists primarily of the Margalla Hills and ___E:Margalla Hills National Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margalla_Hills_National_Park)___ . ___E:Rawal Lake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawal_Lake)___ is in this zone. Zone IV and V consist of Islamabad Park, and rural areas of the city. The ___E:Soan River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soan_River)___ flows into the city through Zone V.

When the master plan for Islamabad was drawn up in 1960, Islamabad and Rawalpindi, along with the adjoining areas, was to be integrated to form a large ___E:metropolitan area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_area)___ called Islamabad/Rawalpindi Metropolitan Area. The area would consist of the developing Islamabad, the old colonial cantonment city of Rawalpindi, and Margalla Hills National Park, including surrounding rural areas.

However, Islamabad city is part of the ___E:Islamabad Capital Territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Capital_Territory)___ , while ___E:Rawalpindi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawalpindi)___ is part of ___E:Rawalpindi District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawalpindi_District)___ , which is part of province of ___E:Punjab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab,_Pakistan)___ .

Initially, it was proposed that the three areas would be connected by four major highways: Murree Highway, ___E:Islamabad Highway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Highway)___ , Soan Highway, and Capital Highway.
However, to date only two highways have been constructed: ___E:Kashmir Highway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmir_Highway)___ (the former Murree Highway) and Islamabad Highway.
Plans of constructing Margalla Avenue are also underway.
Islamabad is the hub all the governmental activities while Rawalpindi is the centre of all industrial, commercial, and military activities.
The two cities are considered sister cities and are highly interdependent.
Islamabad's architecture is a combination of modernity and old ___E:Islamic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_architecture)___ and regional traditions.
The ___E:Saudi-Pak Tower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saudi-Pak_Tower&action=edit&redlink=1)___ is an example of the integration of modern architecture with traditional styles.
The beige-coloured edifice is trimmed with blue tile works in Islamic tradition, and is one of Islamabad's tallest buildings.

Other examples of intertwined Islamic and modern architecture include ___E:Pakistan Monument U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Monument)___ and ___E:Faisal Mosque U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faisal_Mosque)___ .

Other notable structures are: Secretariat Complex designed by ___E:Gio Ponti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gio_Ponti)___ , Prime Minister's secretariat based on ___E:Mughal architecture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_architecture)___ and the ___E:National Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Assembly_of_Pakistan)___ by ___E:Edward Durell Stone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Durell_Stone)___ .
The murals on the inside of the large petals of Pakistan Monument are based on Islamic architecture.

The Shah Faisal Mosque is a fusion of contemporary architecture with a more traditional large triangular prayer hall and four minarets, designed by ___E:Vedat Dalokay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vedat_Dalokay)___ , a Turkish architect and built with the help of funding provided by ___E:King Faisal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faisal_of_Saudi_Arabia)___ of ___E:Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia)___ .
The architecture of Faisal Mosque is unusual as it lacks a dome structure.

It is a combination of Arabic, Turkish, and Mughal architectural traditions.  ___E:The Centaurus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Centaurus_(building))___ is an example of modern architecture under construction in Islamabad.

The seven star hotel was designed by ___E:WS Atkins PLC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WS_Atkins_PLC)___ .The newly built ___E:Islamabad Stock Exchange Towers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Stock_Exchange_Towers)___ is another example of modern architecture in the city.

According to ___E:2023 Pakistani census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Pakistani_census)___ , there are 1,154,540 Punjabi, 415,838 Pashto, 358,922 Urdu, 140,780 Hindko, 51,920 Kashmiri, 46,270 Saraiki, 21,362 Sindhi, 10,315 Balti, 7,099 Shina, 5,016 Koshistani, 4,503 Balochi, 1,095 Mewati, 668 Brahvi, 182 Kalasha and 64,734 others, of total 2,283,244 speakers in ___E:Islamabad Capital Territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Capital_Territory)___ .
As of 2010, the majority of the population lies in the age group of 15–64 years, around 59.38%.

Only 2.73% of the population is above 65 years of age; 37.90% is below the age of 15.  Islamabad has the highest literacy rate in Pakistan, at 88%.  9.8% of the population has done intermediate education (equivalent to grades 11 and 12). 10.26% have a bachelor or equivalent degree while 5.2% have a master or equivalent degree.
The labour force of Islamabad is 185,213  and the unemployment rate is 15.70%.

In the ___E:Islamabad Capital Territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Capital_Territory)___ , ___E:Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam)___ is the largest religion in the city, with 95.55% of the population following it. ___E:Christianity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity)___ is the second largest religion is with 4.26% of the population following it. The Christians are concentrated mainly in the urban areas. ___E:Hinduism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism)___ is followed by 0.04% of the population according to the 2023 census.

Islamabad is a net contributor to the Pakistani economy, as whilst having only 0.8% of the country's population, it contributes 1% to the country's GDP.  ___E:Islamabad Stock Exchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Stock_Exchange)___ , founded in 1989, is Pakistan's third largest stock exchange after ___E:Karachi Stock Exchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karachi_Stock_Exchange)___ and ___E:Lahore Stock Exchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore_Stock_Exchange)___ , and was merged to form ___E:Pakistan Stock Exchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Stock_Exchange)___ .
The exchange had 118 members with 104 ___E:corporate bodies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_corporate)___ and 18 individual members.
The average daily turnover of the stock exchange is over 1 million shares.
According to the ___E:World Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank)___ 's Doing Business Report of 2010, Islamabad was ranked as the best place to start a business in Pakistan.

Islamabad's businesses are Pakistan's most compliant for paying tax dues.  As of 2012 [update] , Islamabad LTU (Large Tax Unit) was responsible for Rs 371 billion in tax revenue, which amounts to 20% of all the revenue collected by Federal Board of Revenue.

Islamabad has seen an expansion in ___E:information and communications technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_and_communication_technologies)___ with the addition two ___E:Software Technology Parks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_park)___ , which house numerous national and foreign technological and information technology companies.
Awami Markaz IT Park houses 36 ___E:IT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Information_technology)___ companies, while Evacuee Trust house 29 companies.
Islamabad will see its third IT Park by 2020, which will be built with assistance from ___E:South Korea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea)___ .
Islamabad is home to many settlers from other regions of Pakistan and has a cultural and religious diversity of considerable antiquity.

Due to its location on the Pothohar Plateau, remnants of ancient cultures and civilisations such as ___E:Aryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aryan)___ , ___E:Soanian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soanian)___ , and ___E:Indus Valley civilisation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indus_Valley_civilisation)___ can still be found in the region.

A 15th-century ___E:Gakhar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gakhars)___ fort, ___E:Pharwala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharwala)___ Fort is located near Islamabad.  ___E:Rawat Fort U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawat_Fort)___ in the region was built by the ___E:Gakhars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gakhars)___ in 16th century and contains the grave of the Gakhar chief, ___E:Sultan Sarang Khan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultan_Sarang_Khan)___ .

___E:Saidpur village U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saidpur,_Islamabad)___ is supposedly named after Said Khan, the son of Sarang Khan. The 500-year-old village was converted into a place of Hindu worship by a Mughal commander, Raja ___E:Man Singh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_Singh)___ .
He constructed a number of small ponds: Rama kunda, Sita kunda, Lakshaman kunda, and Hanuman kunda.
The region is home to a small Hindu temple that is preserved, showing the presence of Hindu people in the region.

The shrine of Sufi mystic ___E:Pir Meher Ali Shah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pir_Meher_Ali_Shah)___ is located at ___E:Golra Sharif U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golra_Sharif)___ , which has a rich cultural heritage of the pre-Islamic period.
Archaeological remains of the Buddhist era can also still be found in the region.
The shrine of ___E:Bari Imam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bari_Imam)___ was built by the Mughal emperor ___E:Aurangzeb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aurangzeb)___ .
Thousands of devotees from across Pakistan attend the annual ___E:Urs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urs)___ of Bari Imam. The event is one of the largest religious gatherings in Islamabad.
In 2004, the Urs was attended by more than 1.2 million people.
The ___E:Lok Virsa Museum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Virsa_Museum)___ in Islamabad preserves a wide variety of expressions of folk and traditional cultural legacy of Pakistan.

It is located near the ___E:Shakarparian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakarparian)___ hills and boasts a large display of embroidered costumes, jewellery, musical instruments, woodwork, utensils and folkloristic objects from the region and other parts of Pakistan. [citation needed]

The ___E:Faisal Mosque U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faisal_Mosque)___ , built in 1986, is an iconic cultural and religious landmark that attracts many tourists; both domestic and international due to its modern interpertation of Islamic architecture designed by the Turkish architect ___E:Vedat Dalokay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vedat_Dalokay)___ ,  as well as its location at the foothills of the ___E:Margalla Hills U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margalla_Hills)___ .

The mosque was named after ___E:Faisal bin Abdul Aziz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faisal_bin_Abdul_Aziz)___ , the then- ___E:King of Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Saudi_Arabia)___ to honour him for his role in financing the construction of the mosque.

The mosque itself can host up to 74,000 worshippers at a time  and its interior is decorated with ___E:Islamic calligraphy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_calligraphy)___ of verses from the ___E:Quran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quran)___ .
One of the landmarks for tourists is the ___E:Pakistan Monument U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Monument)___ built in 2007 located in Islamabad.
This tourist attraction represents the patriotism and sovereignty of Pakistan.

The design is shaped as a dome with petal-shaped walls that are engraved with arts portraying Pakistan's other tourist landmarks such as the ___E:Badshahi Mosque U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badshahi_Mosque)___ , ___E:Minar-e-Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minar-e-Pakistan)___ and ___E:Lahore Fort U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore_Fort)___ .

Islamabad holds some of Pakistan's most prestigious museums such as ___E:Lok Virsa Museum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Virsa_Museum)___ , Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage ___E:Shakarparian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakarparian)___ Park and prominent galleries such as the ___E:National Art Gallery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Art_Gallery,_Pakistan)___ and Gallery 6.

The Islamabad Museum contains many relics and artifacts dating back to the ___E:Gandhara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhara)___ period of the region, an intriguing fusion of Buddhist and Graeco-Roman styles.

The living culture of Islamabad and Pakistan is best explored at ___E:Lok Virsa Museum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Virsa_Museum)___ , as well as the Institute of Folk and Traditional Heritage in ___E:Shakarparian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakarparian)___ Park.

Islamabad is built upon civilization and architecture that ranges from the 10th Century to the modern era. As Islamabad is situated on the ___E:Potohar Plateau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potohar_Plateau)___ , the remains of civilization descending from stone-age era include the Acheulian and the Soanian traditions and these are tourist landmarks.

Islamabad has an array of historic landmarks that reflect the Hindu civilization that dates back to the 16th Century with examples such as ___E:Saidpur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saidpur,_Islamabad)___ .
Saidpur that is situated in Islamabad has progressed from a village to a sacred place that includes temples where the Hindu Mughal Commanders worshipped.

___E:Margalla Hills National Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margalla_Hills_National_Park)___ is located in the North sector of Islamabad and is in close proximity to the ___E:Himalayas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himalayas)___ .

The National Park includes of picturesque valleys and scenic hills that include various wildlife such as ___E:Himalayan goral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himalayan_goral)___ , Barking deer and ___E:leopards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopards)___ .
Flanked by wildlife and vegetation, Margalla Hills National Park also includes accommodation and camping grounds for tourists.
Located in the city, the ___E:Faisal Mosque U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faisal_Mosque)___ is the largest mosque in South Asia and the sixth–largest mosque in the world.
Built in the year 1986, it was named after the late king of ___E:Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia)___ , Faisal Bin Abdul Aziz, who backed and financed the construction.
The most famous and oldest hiking track of Islamabad is Trail 3. It starts from the Margalla Road in sector F-6/3. Due to steep hills, the trail is exhausting to some extent.
The course leads to the point where it goes up to the Viewpoint and is about a 30–50 minutes track.
After the Viewpoint it continues for another easy-going 45 – 60 minutes and reaches the Pir Sohawa, where there are two restaurants for food, The Monal and La Montana .
In total, it is approximately a one-hour and thirty minute walk.
Shah Allah Ditta village is a centuries-old village and a union council of the Islamabad Capital Authority.
The village is named after a dervish who belonged to the Mughal era. It is estimated to be 650 years old approximately.
It is also home to ancient caves that reflects the previous civilizations.
The 2500-year-old Buddhist caves at the foot of Margalla Hills are located in west of Taxila, east of Islamabad and in the central area of Khanpur.
A spring, a pond and a garden still exist near the Shah Allah Ditta Caves.
There are some banyan trees in the garden, while all other fruit trees are gone. The water from the same spring was used to irrigate the garden adjoining the caves.

During the Mughal period, when India was the centre of Sufism originating from Arabia and Central Asia, a saint named Shah Allah Ditta stayed in this garden and was entombed here. The place formerly attributed to sadhus, monks, or jogis is today known for the famous Sufi Shah Allah Ditta.

A short distance from these caves is also an ancient baoli (stepwell) in the village of Kanthila, which is said to have been built by ___E:Sher Shah Suri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sher_Shah_Suri)___ .

Islamabad is connected to major destinations around the world and domestically through ___E:Islamabad International Airport (IIAP) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_International_Airport)___ .
The airport is the largest in Pakistan and is located south-west of Islamabad.
The new airport inaugurated on 20 April 2018, spreads over 19 square kilometers with 15 passenger boarding bridges.
It also includes facilities to accommodate two double-decker Airbus A380s, 15 remote bays and 3 remote bays for Air cargo.

The ___E:Rawalpindi-Islamabad Metrobus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rawalpindi-Islamabad_Metrobus)___ is a 83.6 km (51.9 mi) ___E:bus rapid transit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_rapid_transit)___ system operating in the ___E:Islamabad-Rawalpindi metropolitan area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad-Rawalpindi_metropolitan_area)___ .

The second stage stretches 25.6 kilometres between the ___E:Peshawar Morr Interchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshawar_Morr_Interchange)___ and ___E:New Islamabad International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Islamabad_International_Airport)___ and was inaugurated on 18 April 2022.   On 7 July 2022, the Green Line and Blue Lines were added to this Metrobus network.

The system uses e-ticketing and an ___E:Intelligent Transportation System U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligent_Transportation_System)___ and is managed by the ___E:Punjab Mass Transit Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Mass_Transit_Authority)___ .
The metro buses are widely used for commuting purposes by the labor force and students.

___E:Islamabad railway station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_railway_station)___ is located in sector I-9 in Islamabad, ___E:Capital Territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Capital_Territory)___ , ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan)___ .
The station appears as ___E:Margala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margala)___ on the ___E:Pakistan Railways U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Railways)___ website.

___E:M-2 Motorway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M-2_motorway_(Pakistan))___ is 367 km (228 mi) long and connects Islamabad and ___E:Lahore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore)___ .  ___E:M-1 Motorway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M-1_motorway_(Pakistan))___ connects Islamabad with Peshawar and is 155 km (96 mi) long.  Islamabad is linked to Rawalpindi through the ___E:Faizabad Interchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faizabad_Interchange)___ , which has a daily traffic volume of about 48,000 vehicles.
As of 2010, Islamabad boasts the highest literacy rate in Pakistan at 98%,  and has some of the most advanced educational institutes in the country.

A large number of ___E:public U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_university)___ and ___E:private U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_university)___ sector educational institutes are present here. The higher education institutes in the capital are either federally chartered or administered by private organizations and almost all of them are recognised by the ___E:Higher Education Commission of Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_Education_Commission_of_Pakistan)___ .

In 2008, Islamabad had the lowest rate of infant mortality in the country at 38 deaths per thousand compared to the national average of 78 deaths per thousand.
Islamabad has both public and private medical centres.
The largest hospital in Islamabad is ___E:Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Institute_of_Medical_Sciences)___ (PIMS) hospital.
It was established in 1985 as a teaching and doctor training institute.
PIMS functions as a National Reference Center and provides specialised diagnostic and curative services.
The hospital has 30 major medical departments.
PIMS is divided into five administrative branches.
Islamabad Hospital is the major component with a 592-bed facility and 22 medical and surgical specialties.

The Children's Hospital is a 230-bed hospital completed in 1985. It contains six major facilities: Surgical and Allied Specialties, Medical and Allied Specialties, Diagnostic Facilities, Operation Theatre, Critical Care (NICU, PICU, Isolation & Accident Emergency), and a Blood Bank.  The Maternal and Child Health Care Center is a training institute with an attached hospital of 125 beds offering different clinical and operational services.
PIMS consists of five academic institutes: Quaid-e-Azam Postgraduate Medical College, College of Nursing, College of Medical Technology, School of Nursing, and Mother and Child Health Center.
PAEC General Hospital and teaching institute, established in 2006, is affiliated with the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission.

The hospital consists of a 100-bed facility  and 10 major departments: ___E:Obstetrics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obstetrics)___ and ___E:Gynecology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gynecology)___ , ___E:Pediatric U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pediatric)___ , ___E:General Medicine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Medicine)___ , ___E:General Surgery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Surgery)___ , ___E:Intensive Care Unit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intensive_Care_Unit)___ / ___E:Coronary Care Unit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronary_Care_Unit)___ , ___E:Orthopedics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthopedics)___ , ___E:Ophthalmology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ophthalmology)___ , ___E:Pathology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathology)___ , ___E:Radiology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiology)___ , and ___E:Dental U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dentistry)___ Department.

Shifa International Hospital is a teaching hospital in Islamabad that was founded in 1987 and became a public company in 1989. The hospital has 70 qualified consultants in almost all specialties, 150 ___E:IPD U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outpatient_department)___ beds and ___E:OPD U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outpatient_department)___ facilities in 35 different specialisations.

According to the Federal Bureau of Statistics of the Government of Pakistan, in 2008 there were 12 hospitals, 76 ___E:dispensaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dispensaries)___ , and five maternity and child welfare centers in the city with a total of 5,158 beds.

Major sports in the city include ___E:cricket U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket)___ , ___E:football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football)___ , ___E:squash U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squash_(sport))___ , ___E:hockey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_hockey)___ , table tennis, rugby and ___E:boxing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing)___ .

The city is home to ___E:Islamabad United U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_United_(cricket))___  which won the first ever ___E:Pakistan Super League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Super_League)___ in ___E:2016 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Pakistan_Super_League)___ and second title in ___E:2018 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Pakistan_Super_League)___ ,   and Islamabad All Stars, which participates in the ___E:Super Kabaddi League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Kabaddi_League)___ .
